lines.trans: Go shut down outfits way bigger than ours!
Hey, do you know what specimen collecting is?
Specimen collecting?
I mount butterflies as specimens, you see.
What on earth are you talking about?
Even in the pupa stage, you learn to tell which ones are going to grow big.
So I wait until a butterfly grows to its biggest size, and then I mount it.
Why have you been spouting nonsense this whole time?
Unless the target is big, my own credit shrinks, doesn't it?
You guys aren't getting any bigger than this, so it's curtains for you. Good work.
Pipe down and behave!
If you've still got wings, go on, try escaping. Fly off into the sky!

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: うちよりももっとでけえとこ潰せよ！
examples.trans: Go shut down outfits way bigger than ours!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.
Hey, do you know what specimen collecting is?

examples.text: 俺はチョウチョウを標本にしてるんだよ。
examples.trans: I mount butterflies as specimens, you see.

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 俺はチョウチョウを標本にしてるんだよ。
examples.trans: I mount butterflies as specimens, you see.

examples.text: だから、チョウチョウが一番大きくなるのを待って、そこから俺は標本にしてるんだよ。
examples.trans: So I wait until a butterfly grows to its biggest size, and then I mount it.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

examples.text: サナギの状態でも、こいつはでかくなるなってのが分かるようになる。
examples.trans: Even in the pupa stage, you learn to tell which ones are going to grow big.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: a little while ago; just now
meanings.note: Refers to a recent point in time earlier the same day.

examples.text: さっきは何を売ったんだ？
examples.trans: What was it you sold earlier?

examples.text: さっき電話がありました。
examples.trans: There was a phone call just now.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Follows a number or quantity to indicate a lower bound (inclusive).

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。

meanings.note: Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).
